note: A man left a saddlebag full of leavened bread in the care of Yohanan Hakuka'a. Mice gnawed a hole in it, and the bread began spilling out. On the day before Passover, Yohanan came to Rabbi to ask what to do. In the first, second, third and fourth hours Rabbi told him to wait; in the fifth hour he told him, Go and sell it in the market.
why: The Gemara claims Rabbi agrees with the ruling that follows Rabbi Yehuda on how late on Passover eve leaven is allowed. Afterward it debates whether Rabbi meant selling to gentiles or to a Jew, and why Yohanan could not just keep the bread himself.

people.name: Yohanan Hakuka'a
people.about: The man entrusted with the saddlebag of leavened bread, who asked Rabbi what to do.

people.name: Rabbi
people.about: Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi, who told him to wait hour by hour and then to sell it.

terms.meaning: Bread or food that has risen, called hametz. It may not be eaten or owned on Passover and must be gone by midday on the day before.
Hours are counted from morning, so the fifth hour is late morning, shortly before leaven becomes fully forbidden at the sixth hour.

note: Rav Ya'akov bar Abba visited Rava's house and saw him say the blessing over wine on the first cup, and then say it again over the cup of Grace after Meals. He asked why, since Rava had already blessed once. Rava said that was their practice at the Exilarch's house. Rav Ya'akov answered that there they never knew whether another cup would come, but here the cup was right in front of them. Rava said he followed Rav's students: Rav Beruna and Rav Hananel were eating, served by Rav Yeiva the Elder. They asked for a cup to say Grace, then changed their minds and asked for one to drink. Rav Yeiva told them that Rav had said that once they asked for the Grace cup, they could not drink without a new blessing, since they had turned their minds away from drinking.
why: The Gemara has been discussing the order of blessings at a meal. After the story it brings three Sages with three different practices about wine blessings, and Rav Ashi rules against Rav's students.

people.name: Rav Ya'akov bar Abba
people.about: A visitor at Rava's house who questioned his second blessing over wine.

people.name: Rava
people.about: The host, who said the wine blessing twice and defended the practice.

people.name: Rav Beruna
people.about: One of Rav's students in the story Rava tells.

people.name: Rav Hananel
people.about: One of Rav's students, eating with Rav Beruna.

people.name: Rav Yeiva the Elder
people.about: The Sage who served the two students and told them Rav's ruling.

terms.term: Who creates the fruit of the vine
terms.meaning: The closing words of the blessing said before drinking wine.
The blessings said after eating a meal with bread, often recited over a cup of wine.
The official head of the Jewish community in Babylonia; Sages often dined at his house.

note: Ameimar, Mar Zutra and Rav Ashi were eating a meal together, with Rav Aḥa, son of Rava, serving them. Ameimar said the blessing over wine before every cup, Mar Zutra only over the first cup and the cup after Grace after Meals, and Rav Ashi only over the first cup. When Rav Aḥa asked whose practice to follow, Ameimar said he had kept changing his mind about drinking more; Mar Zutra said he followed the students of Rav; Rav Ashi said the law is not like the students of Rav, pointing to Rav's own ruling on the order of blessings when a Festival falls after Shabbat.
why: Rava has just defended saying a second blessing on the cup after Grace by citing the students of Rav, who held that preparing to say Grace ends one's intention to drink. The three Sages here split over that very principle; the Gemara then rejects Rav Ashi's proof.

people.name: Ameimar
people.about: One of three Sages at the meal; he blessed every cup because each time he had meant it to be his last.

people.name: Mar Zutra
people.about: Dined with Ameimar and Rav Ashi; he followed the students of Rav and blessed the first and last cups.

people.name: Rav Ashi
people.about: The third Sage at the meal; he blessed only the first cup and argued the law is not like the students of Rav.

people.name: Rav Aḥa, son of Rava
people.about: Served the three Sages at the meal and asked them whose practice to follow.

The blessing that sanctifies Shabbat or a Festival at its start, said over wine.
The blessing at the end of Shabbat or a Festival that marks the separation between holy time and ordinary time.
